corpusSummary: The corpus surveys 2026 social-science research on large language models across human–AI interaction, AI as research tools, education and wellbeing, and ethics and governance. It highlights trust, dependency, and social dynamics; methodological use of AI for analysis and governance; AI in learning and health contexts with attention to readability and misinformation; and broader concerns about fairness, bias, and societal impact.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction and relational dynamics
themes.description: A synthesis of studies on trust, adoption barriers, dependence, embodiment, empathy versus humanness, and how social ties shape AI use in daily life and organizations.

themes.name: AI as research tool: methods, validation, and governance
themes.description: Papers explore using LLMs and AI to augment social-science methods, develop coding and analysis workflows, simulate social processes, and address validation, transparency, and ethical governance.

themes.name: AI in education and health and wellbeing
themes.description: Research on AI-enabled learning, tutoring, and health information, including effects on engagement and anxiety, readability, and risks around misinformation and ethics.

themes.name: Ethics, fairness, and societal impact of LLMs
themes.description: Work examining bias, cultural adequacy, polarization, and broader socio-political implications of deploying LLMs in media, policy, health, and everyday life.
